subject: Forensic snapshot access & witnessing for on-prem deployment
messages:
From: Oliver Shaw <oliver.shaw@mediquant.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: Dr. Emma Reed <emma.reed@mediquant.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Forensic snapshot access & witnessing for on-prem deployment

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we get the draft MSA and Order Form ready for our legal review, a couple of specific asks came out from our security and clinical ops teams that I want to document so your team can propose contract language:

- We need a one-time forensic snapshot export of the deployed inference environment (logs + model runtime artifacts) for our internal validation team. This is strictly for verification of inference determinism for regulatory audit.
- A short, scheduled "witnessing" session where our engineer watches the snapshot extraction steps and signs a tamper-evidence checklist. The witness session should be limited to viewing and verification — no long-term operator credentials.
- Retention of the snapshot artifacts within our custody for no more than 45 days before secure purge.
- A narrow audit window (two business days) where fragments of the runtime may be inspected; outside of that window we must maintain runbook evidence that the snapshot was purged.

Attached is the signed NDA (MQ_NDA_signed.pdf). Can you send a proposed operational runbook and suggested MSA/Order Form language we can circulate to our legal and GRC teams? Also please confirm if there are any licensing implications for extracting the runtime artifacts.

Appreciate quick turn since procurement is targeting the week after next.

—Oliver
Oliver Shaw
Director, IT Compliance | MediQuant
From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Shaw <oliver.shaw@mediquant.com>
Cc: Dr. Emma Reed <emma.reed@mediquant.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-19T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Forensic snapshot access & witnessing for on-prem deployment

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary and what we can do immediately: 

Summary of approach (draft):
- Deliverable: a time-limited forensic snapshot package (artifacts + extraction log) exported to a mutually agreed S3-compatible endpoint owned by MediQuant.
- Witnessing: 60–90 minute remote witness session (screen share + signed tamper-evidence checklist). Redwood will only surface the extraction tool UI and export log; no permanent operator credentials will be issued.
- Retention: Redwood will keep a copy for up to 7 business days after extraction to support troubleshooting, then purge; MediQuant retention on its side as you request (we'll reflect 45 days in the runbook).
- Licensing: Snapshot artifacts are for verification only. We will propose contract language that prohibits using snapshot artifacts to train or publicly redistribute models or weights.

I've attached a draft runbook (forensic_snapshot_runbook_v0.3.pdf) and a starter redline (mq_redlines_alex_v1.docx) that flags the MSA and Order Form edits we think are necessary. High-level asks for legal/ops:
- Limit the license grant in the Addendum to "verification use only" for snapshot artifacts.
- Add explicit operator boundary language: "no transfer of model weights or executable model artifacts outside gated verification flow."
- Define a two-business-day audit inspection window and a signed purge attestation after the retention period.

Next steps: if this captures your requirements, I’ll loop in Karthik (ops) and Ben (sales) to firm up the order form and planned canary extraction dates. If MediQuant prefers an escrow-style sealed snapshot instead of direct transfer, mention that now and we can propose an alternate flow.

I’ll wait for confirmation of the target week for extraction and your preferred time zone.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-19T16:30:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: MQ-4521 — redlines & runbook review (forensic snapshot / witness)

Team — forwarding MediQuant's asks and the draft runbook. They want a one-time extraction + witnessing session with narrow retention. Key commercial and legal points to resolve before we send a formal addendum: 

1) License scope: propose "verification-only" language for snapshot artifacts. Legal: need a clear prohibition on training, redistribution, and derivative use.
2) Artifact definition: engineer wants logs + runtime artifacts (runtime-config, dependency manifests) but we must avoid shipping model weights. Ops: can we guarantee a weights-free extraction and still be useful for them? If not, propose sealed snapshot deposit (we create a sealed, encrypted blob that MediQuant can witness and store but cannot decrypt without Redwood or escrow conditions).
3) Witnessing controls: remote screen-share only, ephemeral access tokens, no SSH operator credentials longer than the session. Security to confirm implementation.
4) Retention & purge attestation: sales to accept days and potential crediting; procurement will likely want 45 days. We suggested Redwood retain for 7 business days post-extract for support.
5) Pricing / order form changes: Ben, please advise any additional credits or SOW line items for runbook validation, witness facilitation, and one-time extraction.

Attachments: forensic_snapshot_runbook_v0.3.pdf (runbook draft), mq_redlines_alex_v1.docx (annotated contract suggestions), OrderForm_Draft_MQ-4521.pdf (initial numbers).

Action items:
- Lauren: propose concise MSA addendum language for "verification use" and sealed snapshot alternative by EOD tomorrow.
- Karthik: confirm ops feasibility of weights-free extraction and witnessing flow; recommend any changes to the runbook by tomorrow noon.
- Ben: flag price lines we need added to the order form and whether we can absorb one week of retention as part of onboarding credits.

Thanks — Alex
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-20T09:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: MQ-4521 — redlines & runbook review (forensic snapshot / witness)

Agree with Alex's direction. Draft language notes below (high-level, for review):

- "Verification Use License": Customer may use snapshot artifacts solely to verify system behavior for internal compliance and audits. Customer shall not use artifacts to train models, produce derivative models, or redistribute model weights or executables.
- "Artifact Boundary": "For the avoidance of doubt, Redwood will not transmit model weights or unencrypted executable model binaries as part of the snapshot export. If Customer requires sealed-deposit of full model binaries, both parties will agree a separate Escrow Addendum with explicit custody and decryption controls."
- "Witnessing & Access Controls": "Witnessing sessions are limited to demonstration of extraction steps via screen-share and signing of a tamper-evidence log. Redwood will not provision persistent operator credentials; ephemeral tokens for the session will be scoped read-only to the extraction tool."
- "Retention & Attestation": "Redwood will retain a temporary support copy for a maximum of 7 business days post-extraction to support verification activities, after which Redwood will purge its copy and provide Customer with a signed purge attestation. Customer retention on its own systems will be limited to 45 days unless otherwise agreed in writing."

I prefer the sealed snapshot (escrow) language as an alternative rather than shipping full runtime artifacts. That reduces risk and is easier to explain to Compliance. I will prepare a tracked-addendum draft and a short explanatory memo for procurement by tomorrow afternoon.

Ben: will need the SOW line items Alex listed so I can map to commercial terms (credits vs one-time fee). Karthik: once you confirm the ops approach, I will bake the tech constraints into the artifact boundary clause.

—Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
